evals.prompt: Our checkout page feels janky on mobile — buttons jump around while it loads.
evals.expected_output: Should identify this as a Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) problem, name the good threshold (<=0.1), and give retail-specific likely culprits (a promo banner injected after load, images without reserved dimensions). Should not conflate this with a single-page conversion-copy issue that belongs to cro.
assertions: Identifies the issue as CLS specifically, not a vague 'slowness' complaint
Does not redirect this to cro, since it's a structural/performance issue, not page copy

evals.prompt: Is our site accessible? We sell to an older demographic and want to make sure we're not excluding anyone.
evals.expected_output: Should recommend WCAG 2.1 AA as the retail baseline, and give the prioritized high-impact fixes (alt text, color contrast on price/CTA elements, keyboard navigability through checkout, form labels, visible focus states) rather than a generic 'add alt text' answer. Should connect the older-demographic context to why this is directly revenue-relevant, not just compliance risk management.
assertions: Names WCAG 2.1 AA as the baseline
Gives the prioritized fix list, not just one generic recommendation
Connects the older-demographic detail to real business relevance

evals.prompt: Our homepage looks great but I think our product page is boring.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this is about a specific page's content and redirect to product-page, since website-ux is scoped to the site-wide structural layer (speed, accessibility, navigation), not individual page content or copy.
assertions: Recognizes this falls outside website-ux's scope
Redirects to product-page rather than attempting to answer directly
